  *****NOTE FROM THE CITY*****

Doors to the City Council Chamber will open at 1:30 p.m. for Open Session. Please be mindful that
seating is limited and available on a first come, first served basis.

ALTERNATIVE METHODS
The City provides the following two alternative methods of viewing and listening to the City Council Meeting
convenience:

  ¡  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider
  for details.
  ¡  Live online through Facebook Live, with audio and limited video,
  at https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/

The disruption in service of any alternative method does not preclude the City Council or other legislative body
from taking further action on an agenda item.

Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may choose to submit comments
electronically for consideration by the City Council or other City Legislative Body by sending them to the City
Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To
ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit
comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda
number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments receiv
after 8:00 a.m. and prior to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public record of the
meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate
 comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda
number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments receiv
after 8:00 a.m. and prior to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public record of the
meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate
alternative formats to persons with a disability, as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities A
1990 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and regulations adopted in implementation thereof. Any
person who requires a disability-related modification or accommodation, or translation services in order to observe
and/or offer public comment may request such reasonable modification, accommodation, or service by contact
the Office of the City Clerk by telephone at 310-412-5280,  FAX at 310 -412-5533, One Manchester
Boulevard, First Floor, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA 90301 or via email
to athompson@cityofinglewood.org and aallen@cityofinglewood.org no later than 24 hours prior to the scheduled
meeting.

Inglewood, California
  November 14, 2023

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  November 14, 2023, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
  Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Parking
  Authority, and Joint Powers Authority at the hour of 2:00 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/Parking
  Authority Secretary/Joint Powers Authority Secretary announced the presence of a quorum
  as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman/Parking Authority Chairman/ Joint Powers
  Authority Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor
  Agency Members/Housing Authority Members/Parking
  Authority Members/ Joint Powers Authority Members
  Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Parking Authority/ Joint Powers Authority
  officials and personnel present were as follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/ Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Parking Authority, and
  Joint Powers Authority.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/Parking Authority Chairman/Joint Powers
  Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address
  the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Parking Authority/ Joint Powers
  Authority on any item on the Agendas.

  The City Clerk/Secretary announced that public comments were received via email and
  distributed to the Mayor/Chairman and Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members/Parking Authority Members/Joint Powers
  Authority Members.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  November 8, 2023, in the amount of $4,154,411.02, are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing
  Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Faulk that the Minutes for the City Council Meetings held on September 26, 2023, and
  October 3, 2023, be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.
 November 14, 2023

125  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Claims pursuant to Government Code, Section 913:
  1. Jaime Olmedo for alleged tire damage; metal plate driveway apron (All American
  Asphalt) on January 26, 2023.
  2. Loreto Sanchez for alleged personal injury; sidewalk condition (Pacific Telephone
  vault lid) on February 22, 2023.
  B. Reject Insufficient Claim pursuant to Government Code, Section 913:
  1. Evelyn LeBlanc for alleged personal injury; sidewalk on October 7, 2023.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Reject Claims listed as A-1 and A-2; and 2) Reject
  Insufficient Claim listed as B-1. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – TAXI PRODUCTIONS dba: RADIO FREE 102.3
  (KJLH). Staff report dated November 14, 2023, was presented recommending that the
  Mayor and Council Members authorize payment of invoices to Taxi Productions dba: Radio
  Free 102.3 (KJLH), for the radio advertisements aired announcing the Inglewood Music
  Festival and the City’s National Night Out.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the amount of $7,700. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  RESOLUTION NO. 24-14 ADOPTED – AUTHORIZATION OF THE SUBMITTAL
  OF APPLICATIONS FOR CALRECYCLE GRANT PROGRAMS AND RELATED
  GRANT PROGRAMS. Staff report dated November 14, 2023, was presented
  recommending that the Mayor and Council Members adopt a resolution authorizing the
  submittal of applications for CalRecycle Grant programs and related grant program
  authorizations.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  Resolution No. 24-14 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AUTHORIZING 1) THE SUBMITTAL OF INDIVIDUAL
  GRANT APPLICATIONS FOR ALL GRANT PROGRAMS FOR WHICH THE
  CITY OF INGLEWOOD IS ELIGIBLE, AND 2) THE MAYOR, AS
  SIGNATURE AUTHORITY, TO EXECUTE ALL DOCUMENTS NECESSARY
  TO SECURE SAID GRANTS

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  PAYMENT OF INVOICES AUTHORIZED – WEST COAST ARBORISTS, INC.
  Staff report dated November 14, 2023, was presented recommending that the Mayor and
  Council Members authorize the use of $291,956 of Fiscal Year 2022-2023 General Funds
  for payment of invoices for tree services by West Coast Arborists, Inc. to provide tree
  maintenance and arborist services, which exceeds approved Agreement 21-031
  compensation.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby authorize the use of $291,956 of Fiscal Year 2022-2023
  General Funds. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  2
 November 14, 2023

183  RATE ADJUSTMENT APPROVED – AMENDED AND RESTATED
  INTERGRATED  SOLID  WASTE  SERVICES  AGREEMENT  WITH
  CONSOLIDATED DISPOSAL SERVICE, LLC dba REPUBLIC SERVICES. Staff
  report dated November 14, 2023, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council
  Members approve the rate adjustment for residential and commercial solid waste
  collections, as permitted in the Amended and Restated Integrated Solid Waste Services
  Agreement with Consolidated Disposal Service, LLC dba Republic Services.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MORALES COMMENTS. Council Member Morales, District
  3, stated that 7:00 a.m. trash pickup won’t work for some areas in his district because that
  is the time that some families are getting ready for work and their children are preparing for
  school. He mentioned, for the record, that they are still working through those hours,  so he is
  approving the item based on those conditions and doing the right thing in those areas.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby approve the rate adjustment. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. City Clerk Aisha L. Thompson thanked the Mayor for
  joining her to speak with students at Morningside High School. She stated the students were
  thrilled to have the Mayor at their school, and she looked forward to continuing to  uplift
  young people.

126  MONTHLY TREASURER’S REPORT. Staff report dated November 14, 2023, was
  presented submitting the Monthly Treasurer’s Report for the Month ending September 30,
  2023.

  Mayor Butts ordered the report received and filed.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished
  to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not elsewhere
  considered on the Agenda.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) thanked the Mayor and Council for allowing him to speak. He
  stated that he knew his comment wasn’t Inglewood-related and mentioned a meeting he
  attended regarding homelessness. He questioned if a city was a sanctuary, how could you
  deal with homelessness? Finally, he mentioned how homelessness affects the state, and
  the Inglewood and Leimert Park/Crenshaw area was vital to him.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) expressed his concern about the increase in crime in
  Morningside Park and Briarwood. He stated the traffic through Morningside Park had cars
  speeding and ignoring the stop signs, and no police were present. He addressed the most
  recent breaking into cars and car theft in Briarwood. He also discussed the concern about the
  police department's absence and wanted to know why. Finally, he recommended increasing
  police presence.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in the honor of Davin Talbot, son of Renee Talbot, at the hour of 2:24 p.m.

  Approved this 23rd day of January, 2024.
  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
